summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with a history of severe aortic stenosis, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and recent gastrointestinal bleed was admitted from rehab after reporting bright red blood per rectum. He was hemodynamically stable with a hemoglobin of 7.9 g/dL, near his baseline. Evaluation revealed acute kidney injury likely due to pre-renal causes from prior bleed and diuretic use, which resolved with supportive care. Flexible sigmoidoscopy identified grade 3 internal hemorrhoids with stigmata of recent bleeding as the source; no intervention was required. He remained stable without further bleeding, did not require transfusion, and was discharged back to rehab with instructions to continue hemorrhoidal suppositories, sitz baths, and bowel regimen. Chronic conditions including gastritis, anemia, and a healing left olecranon fracture were managed conservatively.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
